text:
carla: Rolling driver 515->545 to hopper pool in us-west1. After canary 5 nodes, ~15% of H100 pods crash with illegal instruction during kernel load. Observed on dedicated and hosted. Anyone seen this? :warning:

jason: saw a similar spike in eu-west1 this morning after the rollout. stacktrace points to PTX version mismatch in nvptx_compiler, messages like `unsupported PTX version: 9.0` in kube logs

priya: got logs from one of the pods:
```
GPU 0: failed to JIT kernel (ptx) nvrtcError: compilation failed
CUDA Error: illegal instruction
NCCL WARN : transport connection failed
```

carla: summary: SM90 models failing during first inference pass. No automatic fallback to CPU so latency spikes and CPU OOMs. Thinking about rollback vs hotfix.

leo: we tested SM90 kernels with 545 in staging but staging used older CUDA runtime so it missed this. Looks like model PTX baked at a higher PTX target than driver supports. Might be driver minimum mismatch (545 vs compiled PTX).

maya: operational constraints: rollback requires node reboot, will interrupt in-flight work. Short-term mitigations: cordon affected nodes, route traffic to other regions, or enable a runtime JIT fallback that is slower but keeps requests alive.

infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy-972 failed on 10/12 nodes in us-west1-g, created taint `gpu-fault=true:NoSchedule` on those nodes.

ops-oncall: SSHed into an affected host. `nvidia-smi -q` shows driver 545.45 and kernel module reports mismatch with CUDA toolkit in the container. dmesg shows repeated "invalid opcode" from nvcuda.

jason: temporary mitigation: set env var `REDCLOUD_FORCE_PTX_EMULATION=1` in serving runtime for the critical routes — this forces interpreter fallback for PTX JIT (adds ~40-60ms per token). Rolling to a small canary now.

priya: also seeing NCCL hangs on 8xH100 racks, timeouts during all-reduce in two racks in eu-west1. Possibly driver+kernel ABI subtlety. Opening vendor escalation ticket with logs attached.

carla: proposed plan:
1) cordon and drain affected nodes in us-west1 (reduce blast radius)
2) enable PTX emulation fallback for high-SLO routes (to avoid CPU OOM)
3) run driver rollback on dedicated pool in us-west1 (use infra playbook `driver-rollback-v2`)
4) vendor escalation + check model build metadata (nvcc, ptx target) so future rollouts are gated
ETA: 90m. @ops-oncall please post progress.

ops-oncall: cordoned 12 nodes in us-west1 and applied taints. Enabled fallback env on the two critical routes. Rollback job queued to start in 28m. Live updates to #oncall-runbook.

maya: cost impact note: fallback to CPU increases per-request cost ~3x for affected traffic; recommending we flag impacted customers and prepare credit offsets if SLA breaches.

jason: followup action: add model toolchain metadata to model registry (nvcc version, PTX target, compiled arch) so future driver rollouts can run a compatibility gate. Also add an automated smoke test that runs a tiny SM90 kernel on each driver before permitting rollout.

carla: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate rollback and vendor escalation. Keep posting logs here. :white_check_mark:
